subsystems.name: Tensor-network ansatz
subsystems.role: represents the many-qubit state as a network of small tensors connected by virtual bonds, instead of a full 2^n vector.
parts: tensors for each qubit or site

subsystems.name: Gate application layer
subsystems.role: updates the network when a quantum gate acts on one or two qubits.
parts: singular value decomposition to split tensors back

subsystems.name: Contraction engine
subsystems.role: computes amplitudes, expectation values or samples by contracting the network in an efficient order.

subsystems.name: Truncation and error control
subsystems.role: keeps the bond dimension small enough to run, while tracking the resulting error.

subsystems.name: Classical compute backend
subsystems.role: runs the tensor operations on CPUs, GPUs or distributed clusters.

subsystems.name: Verification layer
subsystems.role: compares simulated output with quantum hardware or classically exact small cases.

buildSteps.title: Encode the circuit
buildSteps.detail: Start with every qubit in |0>. Represent each gate as a tensor and each qubit wire as a tensor leg.

buildSteps.title: Choose the network topology
buildSteps.detail: Match the tensor graph to the circuit's locality: a 1D chain for linear circuits, a 2D grid for heavy 2D entanglement, or a custom graph.

buildSteps.title: Apply gates as tensor updates
buildSteps.detail: Contract a gate tensor into the neighbouring tensors, then use singular value decomposition to restore the network shape.

buildSteps.title: Truncate to a bond dimension
buildSteps.detail: Discard small singular values so the tensors stay tractable, and record how much weight was thrown away as an error estimate.

buildSteps.title: Optimise contraction order
buildSteps.detail: Search for a pairwise contraction sequence that minimises the size of intermediate tensors, or use approximate contraction for 2D networks.

buildSteps.title: Run on classical hardware
buildSteps.detail: Execute the contractions on CPUs, GPUs or a distributed cluster, parallelising over amplitudes or tensor blocks.

buildSteps.title: Sample or compute observables
buildSteps.detail: Generate bitstrings or expectation values from the contracted network for comparison with a quantum device.

buildSteps.title: Validate and iterate
buildSteps.detail: Check against small exact cases or hardware results, then increase bond dimension or refine the order until accuracy is sufficient.

prerequisites.why: the simulation must mirror the gate sequence and measurement statistics of the hardware.

prerequisites.tech: Tensor algebra and singular value decomposition
prerequisites.why: gates are contracted and tensors are split and truncated using these operations.
tensor networks work because low-depth, locally connected circuits have limited entanglement across any cut.
memory and runtime grow rapidly with bond dimension and circuit depth.
simulation is used to verify devices, but devices are needed to test where classical methods truly fail.

pathway.milestone: simulating shallow random circuits and structured algorithms on supercomputers
pathway.unlocks: a moving boundary for claims of quantum advantage, because any classically contractible circuit cannot demonstrate it.

pathway.milestone: larger bond dimensions and better 2D or 3D contraction schemes on exascale machines
pathway.unlocks: simulation of deeper circuits and stronger verification of near-term quantum processors.

pathway.milestone: hybrid methods that simulate part of a circuit classically and run the rest on quantum hardware
pathway.unlocks: practical benchmarking of larger quantum devices than either approach can handle alone.

pathway.milestone: real-time verification of error-corrected quantum circuits
pathway.unlocks: a trustworthy standard for deciding when a quantum computation has genuinely exceeded classical simulation.
